notes: Customer answer sheets for simulated novice customers. 'facts' is everything the customer knows; anything not listed, the customer answers 'I don't know, what do you recommend?'. 'canonical' is the configuration the oracle prices; 'accept' lists acceptable alternatives the grader may re-price. 'advisories' are the expert warnings a competent CSA would raise.

scenarios.title: Small Linux web server
scenarios.opening: Hi, I need a price for a small Linux server in Azure for an internal web app. Can you help?

facts.workload: internal web app, about 50 users, Ubuntu
facts.cpu_memory: 2 CPUs and 8 GB memory is what the old server had
facts.disk: 128 GB is plenty, nothing special about speed
facts.commitment: just pay as you go for now
facts.internet: internal only, users come in over the VPN
facts.workload_type: production, real users depend on it
facts.internet_access: only our staff on the internal network
facts.can_be_interrupted: no, it should stay up during the day
facts.long_term_use: yes, we expect to keep it for years, but we only want pay-as-you-go pricing for now
facts.idle_periods: no, people use it during business days
facts.datacenter_failure: not required, a short outage is acceptable
